output.headline: Judge orders press passes returned to CNN, MS Now and Politico, saying Trump ban likely unconstitutional
output.standfirst: US district judge Tim Kelly, saying Trump’s ban on the three outlets was likely unconstitutional, issues a 14-day restraining order temporarily lifting it after the news organizations sued
output.bodyHtml:
A federal judge has ordered the administration to temporarily restore White House access to journalists from CNN, MS Now and Politico, saying Trump’s ban on the three media outlets was likely unconstitutional.

US district judge Tim Kelly issued his order in a lawsuit that the news organizations filed contesting the ban, which the president announced on 18 September.

Kelly ordered the Trump administration to return the outlets’ press passes immediately, issuing a temporary restraining order that will be in effect for 14 days. Such orders are typically designed to preserve the status quo while the court gives the case a closer review.

Related: DoJ defends Trump media ban: ‘Access to the White House is a privilege’

Earlier on Wednesday Kelly had set out the past case law that clearly established the need for a distinct process, one involving advance notice of an infraction and the opportunity to plead one’s case.

Prior cases made clear, the judge said, “before a journalist’s White House hard pass was suspended or revoked, that the journalist was entitled to pre-deprivation notice and an opportunity to be heard”.

The judge signalled skepticism when a Justice Department lawyer told him the Trump administration had provided a sufficient explanation for the revocation of the press passes in letters sent to the news outlets on Tuesday, noting that the letters were sent after the revocation occurred and the lawsuit was filed.

Trump had said on social media that the three outlets “shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES,” and justice department lawyers had sought to justify the ban on national security grounds.

The three outlets sued Trump and other members of his administration in federal court in Washington on Monday, arguing that the ban violated the US constitution’s first amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. They asked for a temporary restraining order that would immediately reinstate their White House access while their legal challenge plays out.

The Justice Department, in a legal filing on Tuesday, argued that access to the White House is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president has the authority to suspend access by news organizations.

The three outlets also have the support of a coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, which filed a legal brief on Wednesday backing them and asserting that “stripping journalists and news outlets of their rights because of perceived editorial viewpoint violates decades of supreme court jurisprudence.”

Signatories to the brief included the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, Reuters, the Washington Post and Fox News, among others.

With Reuters and the Associated Press
